Three commercial models: a Quarterly Retainer at 5,000 to 11,000 US dollars per month over three to six months, a Single-Market Launch Sprint at 10,000 to 28,000 US dollars total for one focused 14 to 21 day window, or an Always-On Coordinator at 2,800 US dollars per month on a three-month minimum, with Southeast Asia KOL fees on top. segments.bc71501af2: <1>The regulatory frame is the global benchmark</1>. MAS is the regulator other regulators read. The <2>2026 Digital Token Service Provider regime</2> closed the cross-border-only loophole, and the upcoming stablecoin legislation will be drafted in 2026. Singapore-published press wins international citation weight that an Indian or Korean equivalent does not.
segments.544925456b: <1>Crypto adoption is the highest in Asia</1>. <2>32 percent of Singapore residents own or use crypto in 2026</2>, making it the most crypto-engaged hub in the region by population share. That is the audience The Business Times and Channel News Asia are writing for.
segments.df5e1cd31b: <1>Fintech capital came back in 2025</1>. Singapore's fintech industry attracted <2>over US$1.04 billion in H1 2025</2>, the largest funding window since 2023, with the Web3 sector taking 64 percent of that capital. DealStreetAsia and The Business Times are reading the funding cycle weekly.
segments.62dd1b23d5: <1>Project Guardian is the institutional anchor</1>. The <2>MAS Project Guardian network now spans 40 plus global financial institutions</2> including DBS, OCBC, UBS and JPMorgan. Any RWA, tokenisation or institutional-DeFi launch in 2026 reads better with a Project Guardian-adjacent angle in the lead paragraph.
segments.5e4de6c8e1: <1>Token2049 Singapore is the highest-leverage week of the year</1>. October 7 and 8, 2026 at Marina Bay Sands. The world's largest crypto conference. Press demand outstrips supply by 4 to 5x. Briefings have to start in mid-August to make the cycle.
segments.7e78e4227f: <1>The wholesale CBDC tokenised-bills track is live</1>. <2>MAS announced at the Singapore FinTech Festival in November 2025</2> that it will issue tokenised bills settled in central bank digital currency in 2026 and is ready to draft stablecoin legislation. Every tokenisation announcement in 2026 sits inside this frame.

segments.7e4b91d7db: The Singapore press sequence that actually works
segments.df79aa7f9b: The home-market-first pattern that lands in India and Korea inverts in Singapore. Singapore press is global press. A Business Times or DealStreetAsia exclusive is read in New York, London and Hong Kong on the same day. That changes the sequence.
segments.bb0ef50c45: A 14 to 21 day Single-Market Launch Sprint for a Singapore-anchored announcement:
segments.3429ea97cd: <1>Days 1 to 4</1>. Pull the Singapore-specific framing. Identify the right Singapore outlet for the exclusive based on the audience that matters (The Business Times for MAS-and-fund-raise framing, DealStreetAsia for the round detail, Channel News Asia for the regulatory and public-interest angle, e27 for the founder profile). Draft the Singapore press kit with the MAS regulatory note, the named institutional partner, the round detail and any Token2049 or Singapore FinTech Festival event tie-in.
segments.a69088a9d0: <1>Days 5 to 10</1>. Brief the Singapore exclusive 5 days ahead under embargo. Brief the Singapore re-report destinations (Tech in Asia, Tech Wire Asia, Lianhe Zaobao for Mandarin) 48 hours behind. Brief the international tier-1 re-report (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, AI Magazine, TechCrunch) 24 hours behind the Singapore lift. Brief 4 to 8 named Southeast Asia KOL voices on X, YouTube and Telegram for coordinated activation.
segments.56a865a4a3: <1>Days 11 to 16</1>. Singapore exclusive lifts at 7 AM SGT on a Tuesday or Wednesday. Singapore re-reports follow inside the same day. International re-report lifts at 9 PM ET the same evening (10 AM SGT the next day). KOL wave times to the international lift. Founder LinkedIn post and X post timed to the Singapore exclusive.
segments.0797eabe41: <1>Days 17 to 21</1>. Named placements landed, audience overlap report, Singapore and regional search-impressions delta, sentiment on the MAS framing, post-Token2049 or post-FinTech-Festival follow-on coverage where applicable, and a renew-or-kill call per KOL on the wave.

segments.ba705f9f9f: MAS, the 2026 Digital Token Service Provider regime and the stablecoin draft
segments.783bd57ff5: Every Singapore press announcement Shilika ships in 2026 carries a MAS-aware framing line. The relevant frames:
segments.cb60f4bc0d: <1>The 2026 Digital Token Service Provider regime</1>. MAS clarified in 2025 that the previously cross-border-only loophole is closed. Press copy for any digital-asset business has to confirm DTSP status, in-principle approval or exemption category in the lead paragraphs.
segments.e4773733b1: <1>The upcoming stablecoin legislation</1>. MAS will draft stablecoin legislation in 2026 building on the Single-Currency Stablecoin framework. Stablecoin issuance announcements have to confirm position vis-a-vis the framework. StraitsX and XSGD remain the published reference points.
segments.6cbfcc5423: <1>Project Guardian institutional partners</1>. Tokenisation, RWA and institutional-DeFi launches read better when an institutional partner is named in the lead, ideally one of the 40+ Project Guardian banks (DBS, OCBC, UBS, JPMorgan and counting).
segments.500074c208: <1>The wholesale CBDC tokenised-bills track</1>. Live in 2026 per the MAS Singapore FinTech Festival 2025 announcement. Any tokenised-asset launch in 2026 reads inside this frame, not next to it.
segments.b7ac605414: <1>IMDA, CSA and the cyber beat</1>. Cybersecurity press copy has to name the IMDA Cyber Security Act 2025 amendments and any CSA advisory the announcement intersects with. The Straits Times and Channel News Asia are reading both beats weekly.
segments.ac3c9af5ae: <1>Field note</1> Singapore press in 2026 wants to know the MAS status before they want to know the cap-table. The Digital Token Service Provider line is the first paragraph, not the disclosure footnote. A Project Guardian partner name in the lead is worth two named US VCs further down.
segments.adf4e8a29c: The AI search layer for Singapore audiences
segments.9583754d7f: Singapore audiences searching in English and Mandarin see a mix of Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude responses on Web3, AI and fintech queries. Per <1>Google's AI optimization guide</1>, non-commodity content with named-expert bylines and strong E-E-A-T signals wins citations on these surfaces, and Singapore press placements in The Business Times, Channel News Asia, DealStreetAsia and Lianhe Zaobao carry exactly that signal. Per <2>Google's gen-AI content guidance</2>, originality, named expertise and substantive review are the bar regardless of language.
segments.8fb51db42b: The <1>Princeton GEO study (Aggarwal et al., arXiv:2311.09735)</1> found pages combining citations, statistics and named quotations get cited 30 to 40 percent more by generative engines, and the dynamic holds for Singapore-English and Singapore-Mandarin AI search too. A campaign that earns a named-byline placement in The Business Times or DealStreetAsia, then re-reports across CNA, Tech in Asia and Lianhe Zaobao, builds the citation graph that ChatGPT and Perplexity rank against on "best Web3 PR agency Singapore", "MAS stablecoin licence" and "Token2049 announcement" queries.

segments.954b00c715: What does a Singapore Web3 or AI PR program actually cover?
segments.6bb536745c: Seven workstreams. One: Singapore exclusive lead with The Business Times, DealStreetAsia, Channel News Asia, The Straits Times or e27 depending on the audience. Two: Singapore re-report wave across Tech in Asia, Tech Wire Asia, Asia Tech Daily and Lianhe Zaobao (for Chinese-language Singapore audiences) timed to lift inside the same day as the exclusive. Three: tier-1 international re-report through CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, AI Magazine or TechCrunch 24 hours behind the Singapore lift. Four: MAS-aware framing baked into every press copy under the 2026 Digital Token Service Provider regime and the upcoming stablecoin legislation. Five: named regional KOL voices on X, YouTube and Telegram with FTC-and-MAS-aware briefs. Six: on-ground event leverage at Token2049 Singapore (Marina Bay Sands, October 2026) and the Singapore FinTech Festival. Seven: founder LinkedIn and X-Asia activation timed to the press cycle.
segments.bffc8c38c1: How much does Singapore Web3 or AI PR cost in 2026?
segments.a8dd88fb79: Three commercial models. Singapore Quarterly Retainer runs 5,000 to 11,000 US dollars per month over three to six months and covers one to two named-Singapore placements per quarter plus the international re-report wave. Singapore Single-Market Launch Sprint runs 10,000 to 28,000 US dollars total for one focused 14 to 21 day window timed to a MAS announcement, Token2049 keynote, Project Guardian milestone or a Series A or B raise. Always-On Singapore Coordinator runs 2,800 US dollars per month with a three-month minimum. KOL fees sit on top. Published 2026 Southeast Asia KOL rates run nano 250 to 1,800 US dollars per deliverable, micro 700 to 6,000, mid 8,000 to 25,000, macro 20,000 to 80,000 plus, with a Token2049 event-week premium of 30 to 50 percent on every tier.
segments.66053eb05a: Why does Singapore press want the MAS framing inside the first three paragraphs?
segments.43eec30bec: Because Singapore business press treats the regulator as a participant in the story, not a backdrop. The Business Times and Channel News Asia read every Web3 announcement against the 2026 Digital Token Service Provider regime, the upcoming stablecoin legislation, Project Guardian institutional partners and the wholesale CBDC tokenised-bill settlement track. Press copy that buries the regulator paragraph reads as either uninformed or evasive. Conversely, press copy that opens with the right MAS frame signals founder-credibility before any product detail. The Singapore FinTech Festival announcement cycle every November is the most-watched MAS calendar moment globally.
segments.f69f8f3b7e: How does Token2049 Singapore change the press calendar for a Web3 founder?
segments.93d791fda9: Token2049 Singapore on 7 and 8 October 2026 at Marina Bay Sands is the world's largest crypto conference and the single highest-leverage week for a Web3 launch in APAC. The press cycle starts five weeks out with embargo briefings to The Business Times, DealStreetAsia and Channel News Asia, lifts on the Monday before the event with a Singapore exclusive, runs side-events and named-byline coverage through the conference, and closes with a post-event tier-1 international re-report on the Friday. Token2049 week press demand outstrips supply by 4 to 5x, which is why the briefings start in mid-August and not early September.
segments.f1c1a3de68: Does Singapore PR earn AI search citations on regional queries?
segments.f84b258820: Yes. Singapore audiences searching in English and Mandarin see a mix of Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude responses on Web3, AI and fintech queries. Named-byline placements in The Business Times, Channel News Asia, DealStreetAsia, e27 and Lianhe Zaobao carry the named-expertise and E-E-A-T signal Google explicitly names in its AI optimization guide. The Princeton GEO study found pages combining citations, statistics and named quotations get cited 30 to 40 percent more by generative engines, and the dynamic holds for Singapore-English and Singapore-Mandarin AI search queries on best Web3 PR agency Singapore, MAS stablecoin licence and Token2049 announcement.
segments.1e02ebd67c: Which Singapore outlets are the right exclusives for an AI startup versus a Web3 startup?
segments.de9a80b62a: For an AI startup with an enterprise customer announcement, The Business Times or Channel News Asia for the customer-name framing. For an AI startup raising a Series A or B, DealStreetAsia for the funding lead with e27 and Tech in Asia as same-day re-reports. For a Web3 startup announcing a MAS Digital Token Service Provider in-principle approval or licence, The Business Times for the regulatory lead with Cointelegraph and CoinDesk Asia re-reports 24 hours behind. For a Web3 startup launching a Token2049 keynote, an embargoed DealStreetAsia exclusive five days ahead followed by the international tier-1 re-report timed to the keynote. For a Project Guardian institutional partner story, Channel News Asia or The Business Times for the institutional-partner-name lead.
segments.e33a9b7fb7: Does Shilika work with Singapore-domiciled founders who actually operate in another region?
segments.3de01585c4: Yes. A meaningful share of Singapore-domiciled Web3 founders run the operating team out of India, Vietnam, Korea or the US. The Singapore PR programme works the same way: Singapore exclusive for the MAS-and-fund-raise framing, then a home-team region re-report wave timed behind it. The brief simply names the operating geography as a credibility anchor (Indian engineering bench, Korean exchange listing pipeline, Vietnamese retail traction) rather than burying it in the bio.
